name: Marba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Franco Nicola 1970, Vocabulaire Marba (214 pp., Glottolog MED doctype phonology_or_text); also Colin Price 1968, Azumeina-English Dictionary
earlier_scan.note: Tonal Masa (Chadic) language; Nicola 1970 vocabulary with phonology plausibly covers accent, not found online; Wikipedia stress section reads 'To be completed'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Marba language' and (fr) 'Marba (langue)', accessed 2026-09-17 (article largely sourced to Price 1968 and the Marba Bible translation committee)
sources.note: 'Marba has three tones' (high acute, low grave, mid unmarked; cited to Price 1968 pp. I, IV-VI); subsection 'Stress, rhythm and intonation' reads only 'To be completed'. Not a scholarly source; recorded for the pointer to Price 1968 and Melis 2014 only.

sources.citation: Melis, Antonino. 2014. Dictionnaire marba-français (parlers du Mayo-Kebby). Yagoua (Cameroun): Centre Culturel de la Vallée du Logone. [Glottolog ref 556634]
sources.note: Only a one-page 'Système de transcription et ordre alphabétique' (p. 1): IPA-based transcription, vowel length by doubling, glottal stop as apostrophe, nasalisation written under the vowel to leave room for the tone mark; 'Pour les tons, les différences de registre sont notées par : á = ton haut, à = ton bas' (two registers). Nothing on stress, accent, intensity or syllable prominence anywhere in the captured text (grep accent/intensit/syllabe/prosod = 0 hits). Live academia.edu page and its PDF attachment are 403 / not archived.

sources.citation: Shryock, Aaron. 1997. The classification of the Masa group of languages. Studies in African Linguistics 26(1): 29-62. doi:10.32473/sal.v26i1.107396
sources.note: Comparative/classificatory; Marba data taken from 'Franco 1970, Price 1968' (Appendix A, p. 47). Appendix B p. 47: 'Tone has not been reconstructed. The tone patterns of verbs are not indicated because tone has a grammatical function in these languages, indicating the aspect of the verb... For the nouns, however, tone is lexical'. No stress/accent statement for Marba or any Masa-group language.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid Marba [marb1239] and its reference list (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: MEDs = Nicola 1970 (dictionary) and Lukas 1937 (wordlist); full list adds Melis 2014, Ajello et al. 2001, Hamm et al. 2000, Shryock 1997, Melis 2006 (on Ham, not Marba), Ethnologue 28. No grammar or phonology of Marba exists in Glottolog.

sources.citation: De Dominicis, Amedeo. 2003. Tone or pitch accent in Masa? In H. Ekkehard Wolff (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics (Chadic Linguistics 1), 53-72. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.

sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; Harvard e-access not checked
sources.note: Not on Marba but on its closest well-described North Masa relative; addresses the tone-vs-pitch-accent question for the group and would frame any Marba stress inference; whole-volume PDF sold by Köppe.

sources.citation: Ajello, Roberto, Mayore Karyo, Antonio Melis & Ousmanou Dobio. 2001. Lexique comparatif de six langues du Tchadique central (Gizey, Ham, Lew, Marba, Masa, Musey). Pisa: Edizioni Plus. 73 pp. ISBN 9788884920041.

sources.note: Tone-marked comparative lexicon with Marba column, probably with a short phonological/transcription preface per language; the only other Melis-team publication covering Marba.
